description: Self-hosted private chat: no cloud, no telemetry, no Big Tech. Discord alternative that runs on your own machine.

latest_release.name: Haven 4.28.0
latest_release.body:
### Added
- Settings are split into a few pages, so each one is short: Appearance, Chat & media, Notifications and so on for you, and Server, People & roles, Safety, Content, Network & scale and Bots & data for admins. Longer explanations fold behind an ⓘ button (thanks Amnibro, #5838).
- AutoMod Quarantine, an experimental plugin (thanks Amnibro, #5836): holds links in chat until they are checked, by an AI model on your own server or a cloud AI a moderator picks. Off unless a member turns the plugin on and, for the server parts, an admin turns on Settings > Safety > Auto-Mod > AI link checks. Only the link is ever sent to an AI, never the message. See docs/automod.md.
- Send later takes files: attach them in the Send later window, and files already waiting in the message box come along.
- Blocked file types under Settings > Admin > Content > Uploads & Limits (#5833): list types such as exe, bat or dll, and nobody can upload files of those types. Empty by default.
- Listen Together plays Spotify playlists and albums: sharing one queues its songs in order, found on YouTube like single Spotify songs. It used to play one song named after the playlist.
- What's new after an update: a popup with the release notes since the version you last saw. Settings > What's New picks which updates bring it up (every update, new features, big updates only, or never), with the parts of the version number that count underlined. The notes come from the server's own changelog.
- A Copy button on code blocks (thanks Roolk, #5844).
- Channel types: save a set of Channel Functions (text, pictures and files, reactions, read only, voice, screen share, music, soundboard) under a name and an icon, in Settings > Server > Channel Types. Right-click a channel and pick Channel Type to give it those functions; the sidebar then shows the type's icon instead of separate ones. Editing a type updates every channel that has it, and changing a function on one channel by hand takes it out of its type. Voice only, Text only and Announcements are there to start from.

### Changed
- One click on a voice-only channel joins its voice, like on Discord. A channel is voice-only when Channel Functions has text and media switched off and voice on; other channels still join on a double-click (thanks Keagan for the idea).
- Login session length moved from Uploads & Limits to Settings > Admin > Safety > Security, where people look for it (#5834).

### Fixed
- Changing camera quality or device several times quickly could leave an older camera running or showing, and stopping the camera during a change could leave it on (thanks Roolk, #5843).
- Installing the voice relay failed in Docker and Podman on a host with Linux kernel 7, such as a current Fedora, with "npm error command failed" (#5845). The relay's build for that kernel needs newer system libraries than the image has, so the install now falls back to the kernel 6 build, which runs fine there.
- In a narrow window, the Get the Desktop App and Android App pills pushed the Join Voice button off the edge. They now shrink to their icons, then hide.
- With a camera and a screen share on at the same time, the camera could show up as the screen share or the other way round, and people could disagree about which was which. Each one is now told apart by its own stream (thanks Roolk, #5841).
- Changing camera quality left your own camera preview blank (thanks Roolk, #5842). People who join after the change also see the new camera now.
- Ctrl+V with nothing focused (after clicking a message or the channel list) dropped the pasted picture. It now goes into the message box (thanks Amnibro, #5839).
- Buttons labelled with a symbol, like the + for Add Server, the × that closes a window, or ‹ and ›, showed it a little below the middle. Fonts draw these symbols low, by a different amount in each font and theme, so they are now drawn as icons that sit exactly in the middle.
- Skipping or replacing an uploaded file playing in Listen Together

detail.readme:
# ⬡ HAVEN **A private Discord alternative that runs on your own machine.** No cloud, no company account, no telemetry, no paid tier. Free forever. ![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/ancsemi/Haven?label=version&color=blue) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-green) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-22%20to%2026-brightgreen) ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20macOS-lightgrey) One person runs the server. Everyone else joins with a code. Messages, files and voice never touch anybody else's infrastructure. --- ## Get started in about a minute **Docker** ```bash docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -v haven_data:/data ghcr.io/ancsemi/haven:latest ``` **Windows**, no Docker: download the zip, unzip it, double-click **`Start Haven.bat`**. It installs Node.js for you if you do not have it. **Linux / macOS**, no Docker: `chmod +x start.sh && ./start.sh` Then open `https://localhost:3000`, register with the username `admin`, make a channel, share the code. The certificate warning on first load is expected, click **Advanced** then **Proceed**. [One-click cloud deploy on Zeabur](https://zeabur.com/templates?repoURL=https://github.com/ancsemi/Haven) · [on RepoCloud](https://repocloud.io/details/Haven/) · [Full setup guide](GUIDE.md) **What does it need?** About 100 MB of memory and almost no processor time for a group of friends. In testing, 1,000 people online at once in a very busy channel used about an eighth of one desktop processor core. The measured numbers, and a one-command benchmark to check them on your own machine, are in [How much hardware does Haven need?](docs/hardware.md) **Prefer video?** Short [video tutorials](https://haven-app.com/tutorials.html) walk through installing and running a server. They are also on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Haven-App_Tutorials) and [Rumble](https://rumble.com/user/HavenApp). --- ## Three ways in | | | |---|---| | 🖥️ **[Haven Desktop](https://github.com/ancsemi/Haven-Desktop/releases/latest)** | Windows and Linux. Per-app audio sharing (send one app’s sound, nothing else), device switching mid-call, native notifications, tray. It can also **run the server itself**. | | 💻 **[Haven for macOS](https://github.com/Amnibro/Haven-Desktop/releases/latest/download/Haven-Desktop-universal.dmg)** | A Mac version of Haven Desktop, built by [Amnibro](https://github.com/Amnibro). One download for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. | | 📱 **[Haven for Android (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.havenapp.mobile&gl=US)**
💠 **[Android (via Obtainium)](https://apps.obtainium.imranr.dev/redirect?r=obtainium://add/https://amni-scient.com/downloads/amni-haven.apk)** | On Google Play, or as a direct download through Obtainium. Native, not a web wrapper. Full chat, voice and push notifications. Built by [Amnibro](https://github.com/Amnibro). | | 🍎 **[Haven for iOS](https://testflight.apple.com/join/ADeG5zRq)** | In testing through TestFlight. Native, by [Amnibro](https://github.com/Amnibro) as well. Until it is on the App Store, the browser works too: open your server in Safari and Add to Home Screen. | | 🌐 **Any browser** | Nothing to install. Send a link, they are in. Works on phones. | Apps and browser talk to the same server and see the same thing, so nobody has to install anything to be included. **Want to look around first?** The [community server](https://haven.moviethingy.xyz/?invite=da0b9be7) is open, no code needed, just sign up. Volunteer-hosted, thanks MutantRabbit. --- ## Why bother | | Discord | Haven | |---|---------|-------| | Hosting | Their cloud | Your machine | | Account | Email and phone | No email, no verification | | Your messages | Stored by Discord Inc. | Never leave your server | | Cost | Nitro, boosts | Free, no paid tier | | Telemetry | Analytics and tracking | None | | Source | Closed | Open, AGPL-3.0 | --- ## What you get **Coming from Discord** - **Import your whole server history** from inside Haven. Every channel, thread, forum post, reaction, pin and attachment. Paste a token, pick a server, go. - **Ferry, a two-way Discord bridge.** Messages pass both ways between a Haven channel and a Discord channel, under each person's real name. Friends who are not ready to leave Discord can still talk to the ones who did. **Talking** - Voice chat, peer to peer by default so audio doesn't pass through the server (an optional voice relay is there for big servers). Per-user volume, mute, deafen, noise suppression, talking indicators. - Screen sharing, several people at once in a tiled grid. Watch parties work. - Listen together with synced playback from Spotify, YouTube and SoundCloud, or a music player right in the voice channel. - Threads, replies, reactions, pins, editing, mentions, polls, search, link previews, code blocks, spoilers. - Direct messages, **end-to-end encrypted**. Private keys never leave the browser, so not even the person hosting can read them. - Rich presence for what people are playing and listening to, via Steam, Last.fm or Spotify. Off until you turn it on, never written to the database. **Making it yours** - 26 built-in themes, a colour picker, an RGB cycle, and stackable visual effects like CRT, Matrix rain and snowfall. - A plugin and theme system, so you can drop in your own without forking anything. - Custom stickers, custom emoji, personas (send as an alternate character), soundboard, avatar shapes and borders. - Server branding, sidebar layout options, font size and density controls. - 11 languages out of the box: English, Français, Deutsch, Español, Polski, Русский, 中文, Português, فارسی, 日本語 and 한국어. **Running it** - **One-click updates from inside the app.** Haven takes a pre-update backup and restarts itself. - **Built-in backups**, scheduled or on demand, with restore. - **Single sign-on** via OpenID Connect, so Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia and Auth0 all work as your login. - **Bots and webhooks** with a REST API. Send messages, play soundboard sounds, register slash commands, join voice, receive signed callbacks. - Roles with per-channel permissions. Kick, timed mute, ban, IP bans, slow mode, automod link filtering, an audit log, and a moderation API. - Guest accounts, invite links, per-channel join codes with automatic rotation. - Push notifications, including UnifiedPush if you would rather leave Google out. - Built-in Cloudflare and LocalTunnel support, so friends can reach you without port forwarding. - Bcrypt passwords, JWT auth, HTTPS, MFA, rate-limited logins, and a disk reserve so a full drive never wedges the server. --- ## Documentation Everything in detail lives in **[GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md)**: setup, Docker, remote access (port forwarding, Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel, reverse proxies), themes, voice and TURN, Discord import, Ferry, encryption, backups, configuration, translations, the bot API, and troubleshooting. Short how-to videos are on the [tutorials page](https://haven-app.com/tutorials.html), [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Haven-App_Tutorials) and [Rumble](https://rumble.com/user/HavenApp). Release notes are in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). --- ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome, including translations and themes. If you are reporting a bug, the version number from `https://your-server:3000/api/version` helps. ## AI usage Haven is built with AI. I'm not a professional programmer. I came up with Haven, I decide what goes in, and I test it and run it with my own community. Most of the code, the server logic included, was written by AI coding tools (mainly Claude Code) working from my direction, and most code review is AI-assisted too. Commits don't carry a per-commit AI label, so assume any part of the code may have been written by AI. Contributors sometimes use AI as well, and pull requests are welcome either way. What keeps it in check: - An automated test suite (over 650 tests) runs before every push. - Every pull request is read in full and checked for security problems before it's merged. - Logins, permissions, encryption and uploads have had dedicated security reviews, and the fixes ship in public releases. - Bugs are reported and fixed in the open, here on GitHub. ## License AGPL-3.0. Free to use, modify and share. If you deploy a modified version as a network service, you have to publish its source. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). ## Gallery ---

⬡ Haven
